top_problem: There is no baseline grid. Every card sets type on its own leading (11 / 12.5 / 14 / 17 pt), so rows 1 and 3 are 15-16 pt out of step across the gutter. Sizing cards to content leaves Cider with 81 pt of dead space while Spirits overflows its padding. The boldest missing idea: make each card a real lotería card, with one dominant cut-paper illustration and the card's name set in the classic caption band at the foot ('EL AGAVE', 'LA COPA'), so the deck reads as a lotería tabla and not as six boxed lists with a number in the corner.
fixes: Set all body type on one 12 pt baseline (item names 12, descriptions 9/12, featured 14/24) and snap every item, subhead and banner bottom to it, so that first items and subheads land on the same y across both columns in every row.

Fix the Spirits overflow (-3.26 pt) and the Wine zero clearance by shortening the NOM-006 lines to one line or taking a 12 pt baseline off the banner-to-rule space, and make the bottom padding a true 10 pt on every card.

Rebalance row 3 so Cider no longer sits on 81 pt of empty card: narrow Cider to the 210 pt width and widen Wine, or pair Cider with Beer and give Wine its own full-width card, so no card has more than one baseline of spare space.

Choose one header treatment: either give every card an eyebrow (Cocktails / Spirits / Beer ...) or give none, and make the Classics banner 50 pt tall like the featured one so 'COCKTAILS' stops touching the banner's top edge.
Make the featured card's item spacing match the rest (4.75 pt vs 10.75 pt now), or use a whole 12 pt baseline everywhere, so the spacing between items is one value on the whole page.

top_problem: Card 3 (Spirits) overflows its card: free space is -3.26 pt and no_card_overflow is false, so the Cognac VSOP line sits on the inner rule. The header system is also uneven. Cards 1 and 2 carry a 'COCKTAILS' eyebrow over the banner name and cards 3 to 6 do not, which puts two styles on one header level. The Classics banner squeezes three lines into 34 pt, so the eyebrow almost touches the top edge. The boldest idea still missing is the actual loteria card: an image-led card with a big cut-paper figure and a named title bar in the loteria convention ('El Agave', 'La Copa', 'El Barril'). As it stands, each loteria card is a bordered box with a ribbon, which turns the numbered-card concept into trim on a list. Measurements: banners sit 12.49 pt below every card top and are centred -6 pt (-8 pt on the featured card). First item below the banner is 13.99 pt on cards without subheads and 28.99 pt on cards with them. Subheads share x = 49.5 pt / 325.5 pt per column. The gap after a subhead-led group is 21.75 pt; item gaps are 4.74 to 4.75 pt (10.75 pt on the featured card). Free space: Classics 23 pt, Beer 35.75 pt, Cider 81 pt, Spirits -3.26 pt.
fixes: Fix the Spirits overflow: rebalance the rows (move Cider into a shorter strip, or pair it with Beer) so no card has negative free space, and give every card the same bottom padding above its inner rule.

Use one header rule for every card: either drop the 'COCKTAILS' eyebrow from the banners and show the cocktail grouping once above row 1, or give every banner an eyebrow; also make the Classics banner as tall as the others so its three lines keep the same top and bottom padding.

Fill the empty space in Cider (81 pt) and Beer (35.75 pt): combine them into one 'Cerveza y Sidra' card, or put a large cut-paper loteria image in the empty field, so each card ends on content and not blank cream.

Stop headers and descriptions breaking in awkward places: rewrite or re-measure so 'NOM-006' never splits across a line (Anejo), and add a no-break space before the last word to avoid one-word last lines.

Push the concept into real loteria anatomy: a large central figure in each card, the ordinal in the top-left corner, and a title bar at the bottom ('La Copa', 'El Agave'), so the banner-ribbon is replaced by the card itself.

lens: palette, contrast, price and number styling
top_problem: The Lotería concept only goes as far as a numeral, a banner and a double rule. None of the cards has a real lotería figure: no portrait-format card, no 'EL CATRÍN / LA COPA'-style caption name, no printed card texture. What you get is six labelled boxes in the terracotta, marigold and agave palette every Mexican restaurant already uses. On top of that, the Spirits card overflows (free space -3.26 pt, 'No overflow: False') while the Cider card is 81 pt empty. Measurements: contrast ink/card 15.6:1, terracotta prices/card 5.89:1 (5.08:1 on the featured tint), agave/card 6.9:1, muted descriptions/card 7.8:1, white on terracotta 6.4:1, white on agave 7.5:1, ink on marigold 7.5:1 (all pass). Marigold as text on cream would be 1.96:1, and the layout avoids it correctly. Price right edges spread 0.0 pt within every card (340.5 / 562.5 / 286.5 / 562.5). Name edges spread 0.0 mm. Printed margins 36 pt on all four sides. Price format is consistent: no $, whole numbers, terracotta Fraunces 600 lining tabular throughout. Item gaps: Beer 30.0/30.0 pt (constant), Wine 30.0 pt within the glass group. Card free space: House Originals 0, Classics 23, Spirits -3.26 (overflow, a measured failure, so criterion 6 is capped at 40), Beer 35.75, Cider 81, Wine 0. Layout's measured_checks block is empty.
fixes: Fix the Spirits overflow and the dead 81 pt Cider card by rebalancing: move Cider into the Beer card as a 'Sidra' subsection (or pair Cider and Wine) so no card is empty and none overflows.

Make the palette do more work: marigold appears only as banner and icon fill, so give each card number its own fixed colour (for example 1/4 terracotta, 2/5 agave, 3/6 marigold ground with ink numeral), and add a pink or turquoise accent from real lotería or papel picado printing so this is not the default red, yellow and green cantina trio.

Tie prices into the lotería numeral system: set prices in the same ordinal style (tabular Fraunces with a small terracotta dot leader or a hairline tab like a lotería card corner) so they read as part of the idea and not only as coloured figures, and keep the featured 14 pt prices from outweighing the 17 pt names.

Unify banner hierarchy: the COCKTAILS eyebrow shows on cards 1 and 2 only, and banner widths and heights differ (199x50, 107x34, about 165x34 pt); pick one banner geometry per level and keep the eyebrow on every card or on none.

Push the concept into real lotería cards: give each card a named figure caption in Spanish (EL AGAVE, LA COPA, EL BARRIL) in a tall portrait panel with a printed-paper texture and slightly misregistered colour, and remove the 'NOM-/006' line break in the Añejo description.

lens: design concept and elevating elements vs the best bar menus in the country

top_problem: The lotería idea is only a label here. What prints is six framed boxes with ribbon banners, which reads as a tidy festive template. The missing bold idea: make each section a true lotería card, meaning a portrait card with a large central cut-paper illustration, a numbered corner and a 'La Copa / El Agave / La Manzana' name bar at the foot. Then House Originals becomes the oversized hero card the eye lands on first.
fixes: Fix the Spirits card overflow (-3.26 pt) and the 'NOM-/006' break, for example by shortening the spirits copy or adding a no-break for NOM-006, so every card clears its inner rule by the same padding.

Rebuild the cards as true lotería cards: portrait proportion, a large central cut-paper illustration, the ordinal in the top-left corner and a Spanish 'El/La ___' name bar at the bottom. That turns the concept from a label into the visual system.

Remove the dead space (Cider has 81 pt empty, Beer 36 pt, Classics 23 pt). Merge Cider into Beer as 'Cerveza y Sidra', or give Cider a smaller card, and give the freed space to a larger House Originals hero card with the tequila and Margarita story.
Use one banner style per level: add or drop the over-kicker on every card, and give Classics the same banner height and breathing room as the others.

Replace the taxonomy lines ('a tequila class under Mexican standard NOM-006', 'a fruit drink of its own, beside beer and wine') with short guest-voice tasting notes, because the copy currently undercuts the premium feel of the illustration system.

top_problem: The lotería idea shows up only as a label. Each 'card' is a boxed section list with a small corner icon and a banner. The boldest missing idea is to make every section a real lotería card: a portrait tile with a large central cut-paper illustration and a lotería-style name ('La Copa', 'El Agave', 'El Barril'). On the phone this breaks down further: the cards are tall text boxes, the featured banner wraps to two lines and the tab bar is cut off, so the phone version reads as a web list in a cantina costume rather than a deck of cards.
fixes: Fix the measured overflow and the void together. Spirits runs 3.26 pt past its padding (the Cognac line sits on the frame), while Cider has 81 pt of empty card and Beer 35.75 pt. Rebalance the rows, for example by giving Cider a half-height card or moving it under Beer, or by filling the space with a large icon, so no card is overfull or more than about 12 pt empty.

Make the header system single-level on both outputs. The 'COCKTAILS' kicker appears only on cards 1 and 2, it crowds the Classics banner top at print, and on the phone the House Originals banner wraps to 'House / Originals'. Either drop the kicker everywhere or give every card one, and size the phone banner so it always sits on one line like the other five.

Fix the phone tab bar. The fifth pennant is cut off at the 390 px edge. Either fit all six tabs (numerals plus icons only, with the name under the active tab), or add a clear fade and scroll cue so it doesn't look clipped.

Push the lotería concept in both formats. Enlarge the icon into the card's central image (at least 30% of card height at print, full width on the phone), add a lotería caption name per card, and use a card aspect ratio close to 2:3 so the phone stack reads as dealt cards rather than bordered text boxes.

Fix the phone-only rag and widows. Descriptions at phone width leave one- or two-word last lines ('large cube.', 'fermented ale.', 'Mexican standard NOM-006.'). Balance the text wrapping or cut the copy so each phone description ends on a line of at least three words, and match the print descriptions to it.

lens: every item and price vs the draft (build/draft_doc.json)
top_problem: All 14 items and prices match the draft exactly, and no item is invented or dropped. The problems are elsewhere. The spirits, beer and cider copy reads like taxonomy rather than guest language: 'a tequila class under Mexican standard NOM-006', 'From the brandy shelf; VSOP marks its age grade', 'a fruit drink of its own, beside beer and wine', 'bottom-fermented, from the lager family'. In the same design, the cocktail lines use appetising bar voice. The flow also works against a cantina. The Old Fashioned leads in the featured prime spot while the Margarita, the likely best seller, is pushed down to card 2. A one-item Cider card gets a full quarter-page cell with about 81 pt of dead space.
problems: Checked against the draft: 14 of 14 items are present with identical names and prices (Manhattan 15, Margarita 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Dry Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13). Nothing is added or dropped. The retired Junmai Ginjo is correctly left off and flagged.

Section order is changed from the draft (Cocktails, Beer, Wine, Spirits, Cider) to Cocktails, Spirits, Beer, Cider, Wine. Putting agave straight after cocktails is defensible for a cantina. Putting wine last and giving cider its own full card is not: the Cider card has 1 item and about 81 pt of empty space, and the Beer card has about 36 pt empty.
The featured card 1 leads with the Brown Butter Old Fashioned. The Margarita, the signature drink of a cantina, sits in the smaller card 2.
Spirits descriptions give no type or age a guest can use. 'NOM-006' is regulatory wording. The Añejo line breaks mid-token as 'NOM-' / '006.'
The Dry-Hopped IPA line drops 'draft' and never mentions dry-hopping. The Amber Lager and Czech Pilsner lines add brewing-class wording ('bottom-fermented') in place of flavour.

Beer ABV, wine region, spirit brand and all pour sizes are missing. They are correctly flagged in missing_ingredients and needs_input, so there is no fabrication, but criterion 8 cannot rise until they arrive.

Brut Rosé is printed with a bare 13 and no glass or bottle label. It sits under 'Sparkling' with no pour label, while Malbec and Pinot Grigio sit under 'By the Glass'. The guest cannot tell the serve, and the open question is not visible on the menu.
The title changed from the draft's 'Bar menu' to 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' plus 'Iowa City, Iowa'. This is not a price or item, but the venue should confirm it.
Manhattan hides the bitters (public_components aromatic-bitters=false) while the Old Fashioned prints 'bitters'. This is correctly flagged, but the two classics read inconsistently.
fixes: Rewrite the Blanco, Añejo, Cognac VSOP, beer and cider lines in guest voice using only the draft's words (for example 'Unaged blanco tequila, clean agave; also called plata' and 'Aged tequila, sipped neat'), and remove 'NOM-006', 'bottom-fermented', 'lager family' and 'beside beer and wine'.

Move the Margarita into the featured card 1 (for example as a 'Cantina Classics' lead or as the first item), or swap cards 1 and 2 so the cantina's signature and likely best seller takes the prime top-left spot.
Merge Cider into the Beer card as a 'Sidra' subheader, or pair it with a smaller Wine card, so no card carries a single item and 80 pt of dead space. Use the freed cell to balance Spirits and Wine.

Print a pour label on every non-cocktail price once the venue supplies it. Until then, mark Brut Rosé's price as glass or bottle, or hold it off print until the Coordinator gets an answer, and never leave an unlabelled wine price under a 'Sparkling' header.
Keep 'Dry-Hopped IPA' honest to the draft ('Hop-forward IPA on draft'), and add ABV to all three beers and region to Malbec and Pinot Grigio as soon as the needs_input answers arrive.

top_problem: Only the 4 cocktails have real descriptions (spirit, modifiers, garnish and method, all traced to the draft or recipe). The other 10 items print taxonomy filler instead of guest-facing copy. Examples: 'a tequila class under Mexican standard NOM-006', 'From the brandy shelf', 'bottom-fermented', 'top-fermented ale', 'a fruit drink of its own, beside beer and wine', 'Dry and sparkling'. No beer shows an ABV, no wine shows a region (Brut Rosé shows no grape either), and no spirit shows a brand or age. All of these gaps are flagged in missing_ingredients, which keeps criterion 8 above the automatic-fail line. Still, half the menu reads like a database while the cocktail half reads like a bar menu. Prices: all 14 items and prices match build/draft_doc.json exactly. Nothing is invented or dropped, and every price is a bare integer. Brut Rosé still has no glass or bottle label, and no pour sizes appear anywhere. Flow: the Cider card holds one item and has about 81 pt of empty space, and the Beer card is a third empty. Meanwhile the Spirits card overflows (no_card_overflow=false, free space -3.26 pt), which breaks the Añejo line as 'NOM-/006'.
fixes: Rewrite the 9 spirits, beer, cider and wine lines in guest voice from known facts only, and drop taxonomy wording: no NOM-006, 'bottom-/top-fermented', 'from the brandy shelf' or 'fruit drink of its own'. Examples: 'Unaged blanco (plata) tequila, 100% agave' only if the source supports it, 'Pressed-apple cider, dry and sparkling', 'Dry sparkling rosé'.

Put an ABV slot on every beer and a region slot on every wine (plus grape for Brut Rosé) as soon as the venue answers, and escalate these missing_ingredients as blocking via the Coordinator. Do not leave them silently absent.
Fix the Spirits card overflow so the Añejo line does not break 'NOM-006' across lines. The simplest way is to shorten the copy per fix 1, or move space over from the Beer card.

Resolve the Brut Rosé glass-or-bottle question and print one consistent pour or glass label on the wine card, and on the spirits and beer cards once pour sizes arrive. Until then, print one explicit 'glass' header convention so the unlabelled prices are not ambiguous.
Merge Cider into the Beer card as a 'Cider / Sidra' subheader rather than a near-empty card. Use the freed card for the 'aged' spirits detail or a featured cocktail, so the prime space is not empty.

lens: flow and section order for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The flow undersells the cantina. The prime featured card (1) holds the Old Fashioned and Daiquiri, which have no agave, while the Margarita sits in a smaller secondary card. Dry Cider gets a full card of its own with about 81 pt of empty space, which makes the Cider/Wine row lopsided and gives one item the same weight as whole categories. On top of that, the spirits, beer and wine lines read like a classification database ('a tequila class under Mexican standard NOM-006', 'From the brandy shelf', 'Dry red wine') instead of guest-facing descriptions.
problems: Prices: all 14 match build/draft_doc.json exactly (OF 16, Daiquiri 14, Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, Blanco 12, Añejo 16, Cognac VSOP 18, Pilsner 7, IPA 8, Amber 7, Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13). No items were invented or dropped. The retired Junmai Ginjo is left off and flagged.

Section order changed from the draft (Cocktails, Beer, Wine, Spirits, Cider) to Cocktails, Spirits, Beer, Cider, Wine. Putting Spirits right after cocktails is defensible for a cantina because it leads with agave. Placing Cider between Beer and Wine as a standalone card is not: it breaks the 2x2 balance and leaves a mostly empty card.
The agave hero is buried. For a Mexican cantina, the Margarita should hold the featured prime spot, or the featured card should be the one containing the agave drinks.

Brut Rosé price has no glass/bottle label, and no pour sizes appear anywhere, so wine prices lack the glass/bottle distinction criterion 3 asks for. This is flagged in needs_input, but it is still unresolved on the page.

Criterion 8 facts are missing on every non-cocktail item: beers have no ABV, wines have no region, spirits have no age or brand, and Cognac VSOP's age grade is sourced from a rhum agricole row. All of these are flagged, not invented, which avoids the automatic fail but caps the score.
The Añejo description breaks 'NOM-' / '006' across two lines. Standard codes don't belong in guest copy at all.
The cocktail descriptions are good: spirit, modifiers, garnish and serve all come from the draft and recipe versions.
fixes: Move the Margarita into the featured card 1 slot (or make card 1 'Cócteles' with the Margarita on top), so the agave signature gets the prime top-left position.
Fold Dry Cider into the Beer card as a 'Sidra' subsection (or pair it under Wine) and rebalance to a Cocktails / Spirits / Beer and Cider / Wine grid, which removes the 81 pt empty card.

Rewrite the Blanco, Añejo and Cognac lines in guest language that uses only known facts (e.g. 'Unaged blue-agave tequila, also called plata' and 'Barrel-aged tequila'), with no NOM citations or 'shelf' wording.
Get Brut Rosé glass-or-bottle and all pour sizes from the venue, then print labelled glass/bottle prices in their own aligned column in the Wine card.
Get ABV for the three beers and the cider and region for Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rosé from the venue, and print them in each description (style + ABV, grape + region).

top_problem: The menu reads in three different voices. The cocktail cards are written like a bartender's spec in guest language ('Brown butter-washed bourbon, demerara syrup, bitters; orange peel. Stirred; over a large cube.'). The Spirits, Beer and Cider cards read like database entries: 'a tequila class under Mexican standard NOM-006', 'From the brandy shelf; VSOP marks its age grade', 'a top-fermented ale', 'from the lager family', 'a fruit drink of its own, beside beer and wine'. The wine lines are two-word stubs ('Dry red wine.'). The Lotería concept holds the page together visually, but the copy doesn't: the back half sounds like a different, much weaker menu. Beer, wine and spirits also miss the criterion-8 minimums (beer ABV, wine grape and region, spirit brand or age), and the gaps appear only in proposal.md's needs_input list. doc.json has only two missing_ingredients fields, and both are empty ([]).
fixes: Rewrite every Spirits, Beer and Cider line in the same guest voice as the cocktails, using only draft facts, and cut the taxonomy wording (NOM-006, 'class', 'shelf', 'top-/bottom-fermented', 'lager family', 'beside beer and wine'). For example: 'Unaged, bright agave' is not allowed unless sourced, but 'Crisp pale lager' and 'Hop-forward IPA' are.

Put missing_ingredients on every item that lacks its criterion-8 minimum (beer ABV; wine producer and region; spirit brand, pour size and age statement; cider ABV; Brut Rosé glass or bottle), so the gaps travel with the data and don't live only in proposal.md.

Give the wine lines the same shape as the others: 'Malbec' and 'Pinot Grigio' stay flagged for region and producer, but the printed line should at least follow the cocktail rhythm instead of the bare 'Dry red wine.' and 'Dry white wine.'.

Fix the Cider card, one item with 81 pt of empty space. Fold Dry Cider into the Beer card as a 'Sidra' subsection, or give Wine the larger card, so the 2 x 2 grid stops advertising an empty box and Beer and Cider read as neighbours.

Label the Brut Rosé price (copa or botella) once the venue answers. Until then, show a consistent visible placeholder treatment instead of a bare 13 under a 'Por copa' family card, where it reads as a glass price by default.

lens: how missing data is handled and flagged
top_problem: The flags are honest: all 14 draft items and prices are present and unchanged, nothing is invented, Manhattan bitters are correctly hidden per public_components, and every gap is listed in doc.json and proposal.md. But the printed menu fills those gaps with filler written like a category database instead of leaving short, honest guest copy. Examples: 'a tequila class under Mexican standard NOM-006' (which also breaks as 'NOM-/006'), 'From the brandy shelf; VSOP marks its age grade', 'a fruit drink of its own, beside beer and wine', 'from the lager family', and 'bottom-fermented' printed twice. Meanwhile the facts criterion 8 actually needs (beer ABV, wine region, spirit brand or age, pour sizes, and whether Brut Rosé is a glass or a bottle) are still missing from the page. The result is a menu that looks complete but is thin where it counts, and it has one printed price (Brut Rosé 13) with no label.
fixes: Cut the filler lines to short guest copy built only from draft words, e.g. Blanco Tequila 'Unaged blanco (plata) tequila.', Añejo 'Barrel-aged añejo tequila.', Cognac VSOP 'VSOP cognac.', Dry Cider 'Dry, sparkling cider.', Amber Lager 'Toasty amber lager.' Drop 'NOM-006', 'brandy shelf', 'lager family', 'beside beer and wine' and 'bottom/top-fermented'.

Block publication on the open items instead of printing around them: Brut Rosé glass or bottle, pour sizes for spirits, beer and wine, beer ABV and brewery, and wine region. Keep needs_input=true and set the wine and beer lines up with reserved slots (e.g. an ABV slot after the style, a region slot after the grape) so the answers fall in without a relayout.

Store every gap under the scorecard's own key missing_ingredients (or one consistently named missing_facts key), split by type (ingredient vs brand/ABV/region/pour). Remove non-guest items such as 'cognac row in beverage_categories' and 'Czech or American style' from the venue question list, because those are data-team tasks, not venue questions.

Brown Butter Old Fashioned has house_recipe=false, yet it prints the method and serve ('Stirred; over a large cube'). Confirm with the venue whether the method may be shown. Also make the dairy allergen question a hard blocker, not a note.

Fix the page flow: the one-item Cider card leaves about 81 pt of empty space. Fold Cider into the Beer card as a subsection (or pair it with Wine), give the space back to Spirits, which overflows by 3.26 pt, and consider leading card 1 with the Margarita, since this is a cantina.

lens: trace printed ingredients, garnishes, glass, serve and the new category lines (gateway log_id 112 rows) to sources; verified via gateway log_id 121
top_problem: The new category lines swap guest copy for regulator and taxonomy text, and two of them cite the wrong row. Blanco and Añejo read 'a tequila class under Mexican standard NOM-006' (taken from the authority_note on beverage_categories 04d72e1f / 9f4dae69, both proposal_status 'proposed'). IPA reads 'a top-fermented ale'. Cider reads 'a fruit drink of its own, beside beer and wine', paraphrased from a Czech-decree note on 5cae8177 and a proposed domain note on 914ea33c. Also, spirit_lexicon 21 still files cider under family 'beer', so the sources disagree. On the citations: Czech Pilsner cites bc899a48, which is 'Italian pilsner'. Cognac VSOP cites d4d63f58, the rhum agricole 'Vieux' row, so no cognac source backs 'VSOP marks its age grade'. Under the scorecard's criterion 12 rule, lines that read like database classes cap the score at 40.

verified: Brown Butter Old Fashioned: rocks / orange peel / 'Stir with ice and strain over a large cube' in recipe_versions; menu_items description 'Brown butter-washed bourbon, demerara, bitters.' Printed serve and garnish match.
House Daiquiri: coupe / lime coin / shake and fine strain; draft 'White rum, lime, and house demerara syrup.' Match.

Margarita: rocks / lime wheel / shake, strain over fresh ice; draft 'Tequila blanco, lime, orange liqueur, agave. Bright and citrus-forward.' Match. The 'agave syrup' and 'fresh' wording is not in the draft, and recipe_components returned no rows, so it is unverified rather than invented.
Manhattan: coupe / cocktail cherry / stir and strain. Match. The draft description says 'aromatic bitters', but the print drops it on the strength of a public_components flag I could not see.
Amber Lager 'bottom-fermented, lager family': beverage_categories 6b92613e (Czech amber lager) and ccbedf84 (American amber lager), both under beer.bottom_fermented_beer.lager. Supported.
Blanco 'also called plata': 04d72e1f, name 'Blanco / plata'. Supported.

lens: description quality and one guest voice
top_problem: Two voices on one card. The four cocktail lines are proper guest copy, and every fact in them traces to the venue's recipes (phg.recipe_versions via menu_items.current_recipe_version_id, gateway log_id 119). Those facts are: Old Fashioned, orange peel, stirred over a large cube; Daiquiri, lime coin, fine-strained into a coupe; Margarita, lime wheel, rocks, over fresh ice; Manhattan, cocktail cherry, coupe. The other ten items read like beverage_categories rows: 'a tequila class under Mexican standard NOM-006', 'The aged class of tequila under Mexican standard NOM-006', 'From the brandy shelf; VSOP marks its age grade', 'bottom-fermented', 'a top-fermented ale', 'from the lager family', 'a fruit drink of its own, beside beer and wine'. That is exactly the taxonomy wording criterion 12 names as an automatic fail. 'Dry red wine.' and 'Dry white wine.' only restate the category. 'Dry and sparkling.' only restates 'Brut'. The VSOP line is also sourced from a rhum agricole row (beverage_categories d4d63f58, 'Vieux (VO, VSOP, XO age terms)'), not from a cognac row, so the source does not support the claim. The Manhattan drops 'aromatic bitters', which the draft's own menu_description prints ('Rye, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters.').
fixes: Rewrite the ten non-cocktail lines in the cocktail voice, using only draft words (menu_items.menu_description, log_id 119). Example: Blanco 'Unaged and bright; tequila at its purest', Añejo 'Barrel-rested tequila, sipped neat', Pilsner 'Crisp, clean pale lager', IPA 'Hop-forward and dry-hopped', Amber 'Toasty, malty amber lager', Cider 'Dry and sparkling', Brut Rosé 'Dry sparkling rosé'. Cut every NOM-006, fermentation-type, 'family', 'shelf' and 'beside beer and wine' phrase.
Stop citing the rhum agricole row (d4d63f58) for Cognac VSOP. Print only 'VSOP Cognac' wording from the draft, or flag missing_ingredients until a cognac row or a brand exists.

Restore 'aromatic bitters' in the Manhattan line. The draft menu_description and recipe component both carry it; the public_components flag does not outrank the venue's own printed description without venue confirmation.

Layout (for the designer): the Añejo line breaks 'NOM-' / '006' and the Margarita line breaks 'citrus-' / 'forward'. The Spirits card reports overflow (free space -3.26 pt, 'No overflow: False'), while the Cider card has 81 pt of empty space. Brut Rosé's price has no glass/bottle label. Rebalance the cards and fix the breaks.

Venue fit: this is a cantina, yet agave is two unbranded tequilas buried in card 3, and the Margarita, the draft's signature line 'Bright and citrus-forward', is not in the featured card. Lead with agave and the Margarita using the existing items, and send the ordering note to the designer.

lens: venue-type fit (Mexican cantina and cocktail bar, Iowa City, ZIP 52240; Spanish usage)
top_problem: This menu reads like a regular cocktail bar with Spanish labels added to the section banners, not like a cantina. Agave comes third, inside a general Spirits card. The featured prime card goes to an Old Fashioned and a Daiquiri, and the Margarita sits in the smaller second card. About half the lines are written as category definitions ('a tequila class under Mexican standard NOM-006', 'a top-fermented ale', 'from the lager family', 'a fruit drink of its own, beside beer and wine'). That is exactly the taxonomy wording that fails criterion 12. For this 52240 crowd (median age 28.6, 29.9% aged 21-34, 47.6% with a bachelor's degree or higher, 11% Hispanic/Latino, median household income $52,960) the menu needs to sell agave and the Margarita first.
verified: Margarita: garnish 'Lime wheel', glass 'Rocks', method 'Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice' (phg.recipe_versions f06abb74). The printed 'lime wheel; Shaken; on the rocks' matches.
Manhattan: 'Cocktail cherry', 'Coupe', 'Stir with ice and strain' (recipe_versions 9fb77eaa). Matches. Bitters left off per public_components aromatic-bitters=false.
House Daiquiri: 'Lime coin', 'Coupe', 'Shake with ice and fine strain' (recipe_versions 14d45e57). Matches.
Brown Butter Old Fashioned: 'Orange peel', 'Rocks', 'Stir with ice and strain over a large cube' (recipe_versions 7095fd3d). Matches.
Cocktail ingredients match the doc.json components (Tequila Blanco, Fresh Lime Juice, Orange Liqueur, Agave Syrup, and so on). 'Bright and citrus-forward' is draft copy.
problems: Criterion 11: the Cognac VSOP line 'VSOP marks its age grade' is sourced to a rhum agricole beverage_categories row (d4d63f58). That row is about a different spirit, so the cognac claim has no real source. Tequila NOM-006 lines trace to beverage_categories 04d72e1f / 9f4dae69 per the proposal, but they are taxonomy, not guest facts. The draft component is 'Tequila Blanco', but the menu prints 'Blanco tequila' in the Margarita and 'Blanco Tequila' as an item name, so word order is not consistent across the page.

Criterion 12: the Spirits, Beer and Cider lines are classification text (NOM-006 twice, bottom-fermented and top-fermented, 'lager family', 'brandy shelf', 'a fruit drink of its own'). The wine lines 'Dry red wine.' and 'Dry white wine.' only restate the category. The cocktail copy has a different voice from the rest of the page.

Criterion 13: agave is not first. There is no agave hero. The Margarita is not in the prime spot. The house cards lead with non-Mexican drinks. The Spanish itself is correct (Cócteles, Destilados, De barril, Por copa, Espumoso, Sidra, Brandy y coñac, ¡Salud!), but it is only decoration and never shows up in the item copy. The banner 'Cócteles de la casa' does not match the proposal's own subheader pair 'De la casa'.

Criterion 14: the proposal's measured check reports 'No overflow: False', and the Spirits card has -3.26 pt of free space. The Cognac line crowds the bottom frame. 'NOM-/006.' and 'citrus-/forward.' break across lines, and 'and wine.' is left as an orphan. Brut Rosé has no glass/bottle label and sits outside 'By the glass'. The Cider card is 81 pt empty around one item. No spirit pour sizes are printed.
Criterion 10: the look is one coherent lotería system, but the copy switches between appetising cocktail lines and encyclopedia lines, so the text does not hold together.
fixes: Rewrite every Spirits, Beer, Cider and Wine line in guest language, using only draft words and verified rows (e.g. Czech Pilsner 'Crisp pale lager.', Dry-Hopped IPA 'Hop-forward and bright.', Amber Lager 'Toasty, malty lager.'), and drop all NOM, fermentation-class, 'family' and 'shelf' wording.

Reorder for a cantina (a note for the designer; I am not changing the layout): put Agave/Del agave and the Margarita in the featured prime card, with agave ahead of brandy, and move the Cider card into a smaller slot or merge it with Beer so 81 pt of dead space goes away.
Remove 'VSOP marks its age grade' unless a cognac-specific beverage_categories row exists; until then print only a draft-sourced line and keep the brand and pour size flagged in missing_ingredients.
Fix the Spirits card overflow and the hyphen breaks at 'NOM-006' and 'citrus-forward' (use non-breaking hyphens or rewrap), and label Brut Rosé as glass or bottle once the venue answers.

Carry the Spanish into one consistent voice: match the banner kicker to the subheader pair ('De la casa' vs 'Cócteles de la casa'), and pick one form for tequila, 'Tequila Blanco' as in the source or 'Blanco Tequila', and use it everywhere.

top_problem: Half the copy is written in database-taxonomy wording, not guest language. Examples: 'a tequila class under Mexican standard NOM-006', 'From the brandy shelf; VSOP marks its age grade', 'a fruit drink of its own, beside beer and wine', 'a top-fermented ale', 'bottom-fermented, from the lager family'. Dry Cider: 'Dry and sparkling.' Remove every NOM-006, 'top-/bottom-fermented', 'class', 'shelf' and 'beside beer and wine' phrase.

Stop citing the rhum agricole beverage_categories row (d4d63f58-17f9-5f5a-3be7-5d3c503c92d0) as the source for Cognac VSOP; that row is about a different spirit. Print only the draft's 'VSOP Cognac' plus the verified glass or serve until the venue supplies a brand or age statement.

Label every wine and spirit price. Brut Rosé under Sparkling carries no glass/bottle label (draft label empty), and no spirit states a pour. Print 'glass' / 'bottle' / '1.5 oz' column heads once the Coordinator gets the venue's answers; until then keep the open flag visible in proposal.md.

lens: descriptions and prices laid out together on the phone PNG (round-5, draft ddc4bb5b-70e6-4581-8aae-1b4042cd75ef)
top_problem: Half the menu uses reference-book wording instead of guest language. 'A tequila class under Mexican standard NOM-006', 'The aged class of tequila under Mexican standard NOM-006', 'VSOP marks its age grade', 'bottom-fermented, from the lager family', 'a top-fermented ale' and 'a fruit drink of its own, beside beer and wine' are beverage_categories path text, not menu copy. That fails criterion 12 by definition. It also splits the voice between the cocktail cards and the spirits, beer and cider cards, and a college-town cantina guest will not read it.
fixes: Rewrite the Blanco, Añejo, Cognac, beer and cider lines as short guest-facing lines built from the draft menu_description words (for example 'Crisp pale lager.', 'Toasty amber lager.', 'Hop-forward IPA.', 'Dry, sparkling cider.'), and remove every NOM-006, top/bottom-fermented, 'lager family', 'brandy shelf' and 'age grade' phrase.

Remove facts the gateway rows do not support. In log_id 116 the four cocktails have no recipe_components rows (ings = null), so 'fresh' (Daiquiri, Margarita) and the added 'syrup' (Old Fashioned 'demerara syrup', Margarita 'agave syrup') have no source; the draft says only 'lime', 'demerara' and 'agave'. The 'VSOP' age claim comes from a rhum agricole row (beverage_categories d4d63f58), not a cognac row.

Make the bitters consistent. The Manhattan draft menu_description is 'Rye, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters.' (menu_items, recipe_version 9fb77eaa), yet the menu drops the bitters while the Old Fashioned keeps them. Print them, or get the venue's confirmation in writing before hiding them.

Phone layout (send to the designer). Stop hyphenated compounds breaking across lines ('citrus-/forward', 'top-/fermented'); fix the one-word widow lines ('large cube.', 'age grade.'); fix the sticky tab bar, which cuts the 5 Cider and 6 Wine pennants off at the right edge; and fix the measured overflow on the Spirits card (free space -3.26 pt, 'No overflow: False').

Label every price with its serve. 'Por copa' covers Malbec and Pinot Grigio, but Brut Rosé under Espumoso has no glass or bottle label, and the spirit and beer prices have no pour size. Use a header note such as '2 oz' or '16 oz' once the venue supplies them, and leave Brut Rosé flagged.
